speaker: Unknown
en: Excited to be here with Jensen.
zh: 很高兴能和 Jensen 一起来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: There has been a ton of advancements in AI and agents over the past year, but few months in particular, I feel.
zh: 在过去的一年里，AI 和智能体有了大量的进展，特别是过去的几个月，我觉得。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've seen a lot of these advancements come in the form of better performance, but at the same time, we've also seen that openness and control and trust in a lot of these models and systems around them has become more and more important.
zh: 我们看到很多这些进展以更好的性能形式出现，但同时，我们也看到，围绕这些模型和系统的开放性、控制权和信任变得越来越重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the first thing I want to start with is how and why are you guys at NVIDIA investing in an open agent ecosystem and stack?
zh: 所以我想开始的第一件事是，你们 NVIDIA 的人是如何以及为什么要投资于一个开放的智能体生态系统和堆栈？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, first, before I answer, I want to congratulate you for all the work that you do.
zh: 嗯，首先，在回答之前，我想祝贺你所做的所有工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, if you look at the last six months, we could both agree that although we've been working in AI for 15 years, the last six months changed everything.
zh: 事实上，如果你看看过去的六个月，我们都会同意，虽然我们在 AI 领域工作了 15 年，但过去六个月改变了一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so all of the technology, all the large language model advances,
zh: 所以所有的技术，所有的大语言模型进展，

speaker: Unknown
en: All the scaling, all of the breakthroughs, all the omni models, multimodality stuff, you know, all that stuff is fantastic.
zh: 所有的扩展，所有的突破，所有的 omni 模型，多模态的东西，你知道，所有那些东西都很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in the end, it was the last six months that where everything kind of came together.
zh: 但最终，是过去六个月让所有事情都聚在了一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now finally, AI is useful.
zh: 现在终于，AI 变得有用了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when AI is useful, every company in the world, every enterprise in the world wants to get their hands on it.
zh: 当 AI 有用时，世界上的每家公司，世界上的每个企业都想得到它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now the question is how?
zh: 现在的问题是如何得到？

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is where LangChain comes in.
zh: 这就是 LangChain 登场的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you always had a vision that the large language model was the essential ingredient, the essential enabling technology.
zh: 所以你一直有一个愿景，大语言模型是关键成分，关键的使能技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in order to turn it into a useful product, you have to surround it with what is now known as a harness.
zh: 但为了把它变成一个有用的产品，你必须用现在所谓的 harness 来包围它。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's so much more.
zh: 还有更多的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So much more.
zh: 多得多的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And back in the old days, we used LangChain to help us turn a large language model into a promptable API.
zh: 回到过去的日子，我们用 LangChain 来帮助我们把大语言模型变成一个可提示的 API。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we use LangChain to build our RAGs.
zh: 我们用 LangChain 来构建我们的 RAG。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we use LangChain to step by step by step, which led to today's agents.
zh: 我们用 LangChain 一步一步地，这导致了今天的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And really what happened in the last six months, the big breakthrough are these agentic systems that are grounded on knowledge that can use tools to do search and has memory that it manages.
zh: 真正过去六个月发生的事情，大的突破是这些植根于知识的智能体系统，可以使用工具进行搜索并拥有它管理的记忆。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it has safeguards and has the ability to iterate until it gets the job done.
zh: 并且它有护栏，有能力进行迭代直到它完成工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it ultimately needed some models that have reached a level of capability where everything comes together into that flashpoint.
zh: 但它最终需要一些达到了一定能力的模型，让所有事情汇聚到那个爆发点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's where Claude Code really kind of brought the imagination of agentic systems.
zh: 这就是 Claude Code 真正带来智能体系统想象力的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: OpenClaw, of course, was a big deal.
zh: OpenClaw 当然是一件大事。

speaker: Unknown
en: All the work that you did with DeepAgents and we use that ourselves and all of that kind of came together and bam, here we are with agentic systems.
zh: 你在 DeepAgents 方面所做的工作以及我们自己使用它，所有这些都聚在了一起，砰，我们在这里有了智能体系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: The reason why we do it, we've dedicated ourselves for many, many years to build open systems.
zh: 我们这样做的原因，我们已经致力于许多年去构建开放系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason for that is because ultimately, AI is a fundamental technology.
zh: 这样做的原因是因为最终，AI 是一项基础技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can only be useful if applied in a whole bunch of different use cases.
zh: 只有当应用到大量不同的用例中时，它才有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, of course, the first use case is just language and cognitive intelligence, and that's very important, of course.
zh: 当然，第一个用例只是语言和认知智能，这当然非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we imagine a world where scientists and digital biologists and designers and roboticists and students and researchers, enterprise IT, all of us could use agentic systems, AIs, to solve domain-specific problems.
zh: 但我们想象这样一个世界，科学家和数字生物学家、设计师、机器人专家、学生和研究人员、企业 IT，我们所有人都可以使用智能体系统，AI，来解决特定领域的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And many of the problems that we want to solve, either we have specialized domain knowledge,
zh: 我们想要解决的许多问题，要么我们有专门的领域知识，

speaker: Unknown
en: That is just simply not available outside that we have to embed into, imbue into our AI.
zh: 这些知识在外部根本无法获得，我们必须将其嵌入，注入到我们的 AI 中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or it's because we believe that AI becomes ultimately great, become a super agent.
zh: 或者是因为我们认为 AI 最终变得很棒，变成了一个超级智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we put it into a flywheel where we use it, it gets smarter, it becomes more useful, we use it even more, it gets even smarter, kind of like us, kind of like humans.
zh: 当我们把它放入一个飞轮中，我们使用它，它变得更聪明，它变得更有用，我们要多地使用它，它变得更聪明，就像我们一样，就像人类一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Learns over time.
zh: 随着时间推移而学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: Learns over time.
zh: 随着时间推移而学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we kind of imagine this future where...
zh: 所以我们有点想象这样一个未来……

speaker: Unknown
en: Where AI has a foundation and the work that Anthropic and OpenAI and Google's doing is all fantastic.
zh: AI 有一个基础，Anthropic 和 OpenAI 以及 Google 所做的工作都很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there's specialized AIs and domain-specific AIs and proprietary AIs that people want to build.
zh: 但有专门的 AI 和特定领域的 AI 以及人们想要构建的专有 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we want to enable that world to happen.
zh: 我们想要促成那个世界的实现。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe digging into that for a second on this topic of specialization.
zh: 也许在这个专精化的话题上稍微深入探讨一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: How exactly do you think it's best to specialize these systems?
zh: 你究竟认为最好如何专精化这些系统？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it going to be purely the model?
zh: 会纯粹是模型吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it going to be the harness as well, the context outside?
zh: 也会是 harness，外面的上下文吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: What goes into the specialization?
zh: 什么进入了专精化？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, the specialization starts with you need to have intelligence that's good enough.
zh: 嗯，专精化始于你需要足够好的智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is why we worked on Nemotron and really love the fact that you're part of the founding team of Nemotron Coalition.
zh: 这就是我们研究 Nemotron 的原因，并且真的很高兴你是 Nemotron Coalition 的创始团队的一员。

speaker: Unknown
en: We made Nemotron Ultra pretty incredible.
zh: 我们让 Nemotron Ultra 非常不可思议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, Nemotron Ultra is a great model as a start, but it becomes an incredible model when you put the LangChain framework around it, the LangChain harness around it, so that you ground it on information that is domain-specific.
zh: 现在，Nemotron Ultra 作为一个开始是一个很棒的模型，但当你把 LangChain 框架放在它周围，把 LangChain harness 放在它周围时，它就变成了一个不可思议的模型，以便你将其植根于特定领域的信息中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And an intelligent person becomes super useful when we give them access to particularly important information.
zh: 当我们赋予一个聪明人获取特别重要信息的权限时，他就会变得超级有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so access to information is important.
zh: 所以获取信息是很重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Putting it into a flywheel where maybe you're even training the model, post-training the model, inside the LangChain harness against the harness so that the model becomes good at applying the harness around it.
zh: 把它变成一个飞轮，也许你甚至在 LangChain harness 内部训练模型、后训练模型，针对 harness 进行训练，以便模型擅长应用周围的 harness。

speaker: Unknown
en: What you want it to do for that task.
zh: 你希望它为该任务做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: What you want it to do, yeah.
zh: 你希望它做什么，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think that this moment has now arrived, but we need...
zh: 所以我认为这一时刻现在已经到来了，但我们需要……

speaker: Unknown
en: A open harnessing system that we can build ourselves, that we can apply, and then, of course, improve against over time.
zh: 一个开放的 harness 系统，我们可以自己构建，可以应用，然后当然随着时间的推移进行改进。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love what you said about the model being good enough.
zh: 我喜欢你说的关于模型已经足够好的那部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like that threshold was crossed, I don't know, maybe a year ago by some of the Frontier models, six months ago by some of the Open Weight models.
zh: 我感觉那个门槛已经被跨越了，我不知道，可能是一年前由一些 Frontier 模型跨越的，六个月前由一些 Open Weight 模型跨越的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You talked about Nemotron 3 Ultra.
zh: 你谈到了 Nemotron 3 Ultra。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've done a lot of work with that to make that really good in deep agents.
zh: 我们为此做了很多工作，使其在 deep agents 中真正表现出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of the things we did is tweak the harness to make it best for this model because we found that different models need different prompts, different tools.
zh: 我们做的一些事情是调整 harness 以使其最适合该模型，因为我们发现不同的模型需要不同的提示词，不同的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with that tweaking, we managed to get Nemotron 3 Ultra in deep agents.
zh: 通过这种调整，我们设法让 Nemotron 3 Ultra 在 deep agents 中……

speaker: Unknown
en: We have an internal benchmark and it managed to get up to like 86% on that.
zh: 我们有一个内部基准测试，它设法达到了大约 86% 的水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: Claude Opus for comparisons at 87.
zh: Claude Opus 相比之下是 87。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've got DeepSeq and one of the Minimax models at like 82, 83 down there.
zh: 你有 DeepSeq 和 Minimax 的某个模型，大约 82、83 在下面。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're starting to see that some of the more recent OpenWave models are really getting to frontier performance.
zh: 所以我们开始看到一些最近的 OpenWave 模型真正达到了 frontier 性能。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know.
zh: 我知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am so proud.
zh: 我太骄傲了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is so incredible.
zh: 这太不可思议了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is so incredible.
zh: 这太不可思议了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The just as important thing is it's 10 times as cheap as Opus.
zh: 同样重要的事情是，它的成本只有 Opus 的十分之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think open weight models are starting to really strike a good balance between performance and cost.
zh: 我认为开源权重模型开始真正在性能和成本之间取得良好的平衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'd be curious how you see this cost part changing the equation for builders.
zh: 所以我很好奇你是如何看待这个成本因素改变建设者的算式的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The benefit of cost, it comes in a couple of different ways.
zh: 成本的好处，它以几种不同的方式体现。

speaker: Unknown
en: I happen to think that when you have cost-effective intelligence, people just use more of it.
zh: 我恰好认为当你具有成本效益的智能时，人们只会更多地使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you have a cost-effective agent,
zh: 当你具有成本效益的智能体时，

speaker: Unknown
en: Then you can iterate across a larger search space.
zh: 然后你可以在更大的搜索空间中进行迭代。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as a result, the answer could actually be better.
zh: 因此，答案实际上可能会更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in the case of Nemotron, it's cost effective because it's so fast.
zh: 就 Nemotron 而言，它具有成本效益是因为它非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's so computationally efficient.
zh: 它的计算效率非常高。

speaker: Unknown
en: When it's computationally efficient, it could explore larger spaces.
zh: 当计算效率高时，它可以探索更大的空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's no different than when somebody can think fast, you could explore more space.
zh: 这就像一个人能思考得很快一样，没有区别，你可以探索更多的空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you can try things more quickly, you can find a better answer.
zh: 当你能更快地尝试事情时，你可以找到更好的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this is the incredible benefit of Nemotron 3 Ultra inside the LangChain framework and the LangChain harness inside DeepAgent.
zh: 所以这就是 Nemotron 3 Ultra 在 DeepAgent 内部的 LangChain 框架和 LangChain harness 中的不可思议的好处。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could think so quickly.
zh: 它可以思考得如此之快。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could explore so quickly.
zh: 它可以探索得如此之快。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could iterate so quickly and efficiently that it's going to find better answers.
zh: 它可以如此快速高效地迭代，以至于它将找到更好的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I'm just really, really excited that we created a model that was near the frontier.
zh: 所以我真的真的很兴奋，我们创造了一个接近 frontier 的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: But adapting the environment around Nemotron, you made it deliver frontier capabilities.
zh: 但是通过调整 Nemotron 周围的环境，你让它交付了 frontier 能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, insight, you know, for humans, it's kind of the same.
zh: 现在，洞察，你知道，对于人类来说，这有点是一样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course, we like to hire the smartest people in the world.
zh: 当然，我们喜欢雇佣世界上最聪明的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But beyond that, we also give them access to tools.
zh: 但除此之外，我们还赋予他们使用工具的权限。

speaker: Unknown
en: We give them access to information.
zh: 我们赋予他们获取信息的权限。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we also create the world around them so that we, you know, we allow them, enable them to create the conditions for them to achieve their full potential.
zh: 我们还在他们周围创造世界，以便我们，你知道，我们允许他们，使他们能够创造条件让他们发挥全部潜力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you adjust the environment, not just the model.
zh: 所以你调整的是环境，不仅仅是模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is where LangChain came in.
zh: 这就是 LangChain 介入的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: what you said about using more of the intelligence as it's cheaper and faster we we see that to be so true i think one of the things that i like i like to think i'm ai forward one of the things that i've underestimated is just the demand for intelligence and for tokens and how big and massive that market is and i think that's become especially true recently
zh: 你说的关于因为智能更便宜更快速而更多地使用智能，我们，我们看到了那是如此真实，我想我想我是一件事之一，我想我认为我是 AI 先行的，我低估的事情之一只是对智能和对 token 的需求，以及那个市场是多么巨大和庞大，我认为这最近变得尤其真实

speaker: Unknown
en: With these models getting good and being really fast and really cheap, how should we think about using frontier models?
zh: 随着这些模型变好，并且变得非常快和非常便宜，我们应该如何思考使用 frontier 模型？

speaker: Unknown
en: Should we just use these open source models all the time?
zh: 我们应该一直使用这些开源模型吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there a time and place for both?
zh: 是否有同时适用两者的时间和地点？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, the frontier models are getting better all the time, and I fully expect the frontier models to be unbelievably good.
zh: 嗯，前沿模型一直在变得更好，我完全期待前沿模型会变得难以置信地好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they still have a long, long runway of improving the models.
zh: 而且它们还有很长、很长的改进模型的跑道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Scaling laws, of course, are going to sustain.
zh: 缩放定律，当然，会持续下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Their harnesses are improving all the time.
zh: 它们的挽具一直在改进。

speaker: Unknown
en: Their technology for dealing with memory, whether it's working memory or long-term memory, is advancing incredibly quickly.
zh: 它们处理内存的技术，无论是工作内存还是长期记忆，都在以令人难以置信的速度快速发展。

speaker: Unknown
en: The compaction technologies, all of the advancements in retrieval, retrieval augmented generation.
zh: 紧凑技术，检索、检索增强生成的所有进步。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's still a lot of incredible advances that are being implemented into these frontier model APIs.
zh: 仍有大量令人难以置信的进步正在被实施到这些前沿模型 API 中。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way I think about it is, frankly, I always start all of my work starting with the frontier.
zh: 我思考它的方式是，坦率地说，我总是从前沿开始我所有的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason for that is because it's useful.
zh: 这样做的原因是因为它很有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know what's the potential.
zh: 我知道潜力是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: It costs a little bit more money, but it's incredibly, my time to getting the work done is fast.
zh: 它的花费稍微多一点，但它难以置信地，我完成工作的时间很快。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, over time, I find that I want to add subagents to them.
zh: 你知道，随着时间的推移，我发现我想给它们添加子智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to connect subagents that are super agents at certain skills.
zh: 我想连接在特定技能上是超级智能体的子智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we have, you know, we have optimization problems inside our company that relates to supply chain.
zh: 所以我们有，你知道，我们公司内部有与供应链相关的优化问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe it's related to chip design optimization, floor planning optimization.
zh: 也许它与芯片设计优化、布线规划优化有关。

speaker: Unknown
en: And these problems, these optimization problems are insanely hard.
zh: 这些问题，这些优化问题难得要命。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you're not going to just have a general AI go off and crunch on it.
zh: 所以你不能只是让一个通用 AI 去计算它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And think that you're going to find a great answer.
zh: 并认为你会找到一个很好的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we create super sub-agents.
zh: 所以我们创建超级子智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And these super sub-agents we would create with deep agents, LangChain deep agents, with Nemotron 3 inside.
zh: 这些超级子智能体我们将使用 LangChain 深度智能体、内部包含 Nemotron 3 的深度智能体来创建。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we'll even connect them to specialized tools.
zh: 我们甚至会将它们连接到专门的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that thing is built for one job.
zh: 那个东西是为一份工作而构建的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That super agent is not trying to book me travel appointments.
zh: 那个超级智能体不试图为我预订旅行约会。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just trying to optimize our supply chain.
zh: 它只是试图优化我们的供应链。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in that case, I really do need to have LangChain.
zh: 在那种情况下，我真的确实需要拥有 LangChain。

speaker: Unknown
en: I really do need to have Nemotron 3 Ultra.
zh: 我真的确实需要拥有 Nemotron 3 Ultra。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I connect it to a lot of proprietary knowledge and proprietary skills.
zh: 我将它连接到大量专有知识和专有技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've got a whole team who's just dedicated to refining that.
zh: 我有一整个团队专门致力于完善它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, I think that that defines a company.
zh: 现在，我认为那定义了一家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: A company is really about a collection of a whole bunch of these super, super proprietary, super important workflows.
zh: 一家公司实际上是关于一堆这些超级、超级专有、超级重要的工作流程的集合。
